title: Diagnosis and transfer of expressions

worked_examples.q: A learner writes 3x+2y=5xy. Identify the first error and give the correct expression.

steps.title: Compare variable labels
steps.action: Move x and y terms into separate lanes.
steps.narration: An x tile cannot be counted as a y tile.

steps.title: Repair the first error
steps.action: Keep the two unlike groups separate.
steps.narration: Adding the coefficients does not multiply the variables.

worked_examples.verify: At x=1,y=2, original is 7 while claimed 5xy is 10.
worked_examples.misconception: The learner treats unlike terms as like terms.
worked_examples.repair: Use two labelled lanes, then test one input.

worked_examples.q: A learner simplifies 7a-3a as 10a. Identify the first error and simplify.

steps.title: Carry the sign
steps.action: Put plus seven and minus three on the a lane.
steps.narration: The minus sign belongs to three a.

steps.title: Combine signed counts
steps.action: Seven minus three copies leaves four copies.
steps.narration: Only the a coefficients change.

worked_examples.verify: At a=2 the original gives 14−6=8, and 4a=8.
worked_examples.misconception: The learner changes subtraction into addition.
worked_examples.repair: Attach the sign to each term before moving tiles.

worked_examples.q: A learner writes (2x)(3x)=6x. Find the first error and correct the product.
worked_examples.answer: 6x²; multiply both coefficients and both x factors.

steps.title: Multiply numbers
steps.action: Group the two numeric factors into six.
steps.narration: The variable factors still have to be multiplied.

steps.title: Multiply variables
steps.action: Two copies of x produce x squared.
steps.narration: One x factor must not disappear.

steps.title: Join both products
steps.action: Place six beside x squared.
steps.narration: Every factor in the original is represented.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner drops one variable factor.
worked_examples.repair: Use separate number and variable factor rows.

worked_examples.q: A learner writes 3(x+4)=3x+4. Mark the first invalid move and expand correctly.

steps.title: Trace first arrow
steps.action: Connect three to x.
steps.narration: The first product is three x.

steps.title: Trace missing arrow
steps.action: Connect the same three to four.
steps.narration: The outside factor multiplies every bracket term.

steps.title: Combine two paths
steps.action: Write both products with their signs.
steps.narration: The original sum is preserved.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner multiplies only the first bracket term.
worked_examples.repair: Draw one arrow from the outside factor to each term.

worked_examples.skill: Repair a sign after bracket subtraction
worked_examples.q: A learner simplifies 5p-(2p-3) to 3p-3. Locate the first wrong sign and simplify.

model.description: Repair a sign after bracket subtraction

steps.title: Reverse both signs
steps.action: Apply minus one to two p and minus three.
steps.narration: Subtracting negative three adds three.

steps.title: Rewrite all signed terms
steps.action: Keep five p and the converted bracket.
steps.narration: Do not change the earlier five p.

steps.title: Collect like terms
steps.action: Five p minus two p gives three p.
steps.narration: The constant plus three remains.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner leaves the inner negative three unchanged.
worked_examples.repair: Show the minus-one arrows to both bracket terms.

worked_examples.q: A learner claims (12m+8)/4=3m+8. Locate the first missed division and correct it.

steps.title: Split the numerator
steps.action: Place the common divisor under each numerator term.
steps.narration: A denominator divides the entire numerator.

steps.title: Divide the constant
steps.action: Eight shared in four equal groups gives two.
steps.narration: The original eight is not carried through unchanged.

steps.title: Join the quotients
steps.action: Keep the plus sign between three m and two.
steps.narration: Each original term has a matching quotient.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner divides only the variable term.
worked_examples.repair: Use separate quotient lanes for each numerator term.

worked_examples.skill: Check exponent scope with a negative input
worked_examples.q: A learner substitutes x=−3 into 2x² and writes (2×−3)²=36. Find the first error and evaluate.

model.description: Check exponent scope with a negative input

steps.title: Mark the exponent base
steps.action: The exponent belongs to x, not to two x.
steps.narration: The coefficient stays outside the square.

steps.title: Square the signed input
steps.action: Negative three times negative three gives positive nine.
steps.narration: Brackets keep the negative input together.

steps.title: Multiply by two
steps.action: Two groups of nine give eighteen.
steps.narration: Squaring the whole product would be a different expression.

worked_examples.verify: At x=−3, 2x²=2(9)=18; (2x)²=36 belongs to a different rule.
worked_examples.misconception: The learner squares the coefficient as well as x.
worked_examples.repair: Circle just the exponent base before substituting.

worked_examples.q: A learner says √(t²)=t for every real t. Diagnose the first false claim and write the correct result.

steps.title: Choose a negative test
steps.action: Negative five is allowed as an input.
steps.narration: A universal claim must work for negative values too.

steps.title: Square then root
steps.action: The square is twenty five; its principal square root is five.
steps.narration: The square root symbol selects a nonnegative output.

steps.title: Repair the universal rule
steps.action: Absolute value produces five for negative five.
steps.narration: The output is magnitude for either sign.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner assumes the principal root preserves a negative sign.
worked_examples.repair: Show paired +5 and −5 inputs mapping to the same square.

worked_examples.q: A learner claims 2(x+5) and 2x+5 are equivalent. Find a counterexample and the correct expansion.

steps.title: Test the first path
steps.action: One plus five gives six, then times two gives twelve.
steps.narration: Apply the bracket before the outside factor.

steps.title: Test the second path
steps.action: Two times one plus five gives seven.
steps.narration: The two stated forms disagree.

steps.title: Repair the expansion
steps.action: The outside two also multiplies five.
steps.narration: A correct equivalent form gives twelve for this test.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner omits the second distribution branch.
worked_examples.repair: Keep two paths visible and compare the same input.

worked_examples.skill: Find the first bad line in mixed algebra
worked_examples.q: A learner writes 4(2y−1)−3y → 8y−1−3y → 5y−1. Identify the first invalid arrow and simplify.

model.description: Find the first bad line in mixed algebra

states: First invalid arrow was the missed 4×(−1)

steps.title: Repair the first arrow
steps.action: Four times two y is eight y; four times minus one is minus four.
steps.narration: The claimed line forgot the second product.

steps.title: Collect after repair
steps.action: Eight y minus three y leaves five y.
steps.narration: Keep the repaired constant minus four.

steps.title: Name the error location
steps.action: The initial expansion is where the work first diverges.
steps.narration: A later line cannot repair an earlier wrong constant by itself.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner notices the last line but misses the first illegal distribution.
worked_examples.repair: Compare consecutive lines and stop at the earliest invalid arrow.

worked_examples.skill: Protect a zero divisor while simplifying
worked_examples.q: A learner simplifies (6a²+9a)/(3a) to 2a+3 and says it works at a=0. Identify the first false domain claim.
worked_examples.answer: 2a+3 for a≠0; the original is undefined at a=0.

model.description: Protect a zero divisor while simplifying

steps.title: Inspect the original denominator
steps.action: Three a cannot equal zero.
steps.narration: At zero the original quotient does not exist.

steps.title: Separate two legal quotients
steps.action: Only after excluding zero divide each numerator term.
steps.narration: Cancellation requires the divisor to be nonzero.

steps.title: Carry the restriction
steps.action: The shortened expression is valid only for nonzero a.
steps.narration: A simplified formula does not restore the removed input.

worked_examples.verify: At a=2 original (24+18)/6=7; 2a+3=7; at zero original has denominator zero.
worked_examples.misconception: The learner cancels a then admits a forbidden input.
worked_examples.repair: Mark the domain gate before cancelling any factor.

worked_examples.skill: Audit units and a fixed fee
worked_examples.q: A courier charges R12 once plus R4 per kilometre. A learner writes C(k)=16k. Find the first modelling error and cost for 5 km.

model.description: Audit units and a fixed fee

states: Fixed R12 and R4 per kilometre; learner writes 16k
Variable portion after k km is 4k

steps.title: Count repeated charges
steps.action: Four rand repeats for every kilometre.
steps.narration: The twelve-rand fee is not a price per kilometre.

steps.title: Add the fixed fee once
steps.action: Keep the fixed tile outside the kilometre groups.
steps.narration: The total cost is twelve plus four k.

steps.title: Check five kilometres
steps.action: Five kilometre tiles total twenty rand; add twelve.
steps.narration: Thirty two rand follows from the original charges.

worked_examples.verify: For zero kilometres cost is R12, not R0; for five kilometres cost is R32.
worked_examples.misconception: The learner repeats a once-only charge.
worked_examples.repair: Build separate fixed and repeating rows, labelled rand and kilometre.

worked_examples.skill: Diagnose an area model after substitution
worked_examples.q: A rectangle has sides (x+2) cm and 3 cm. A learner writes area 3x+2 cm² and gets 14 cm² at x=4. Find the first error and correct both.
worked_examples.answer: Area 3x+6 cm²; at x=4 it is 18 cm².

model.description: Diagnose an area model after substitution

states: Split length into x and 2; both share width 3
At x=4, sides 6 cm and 3 cm give 18 cm²

steps.title: Draw the split rectangle
steps.action: Split the x-plus-two side into x and two.
steps.narration: Both regions still have width three.

steps.title: Calculate both regions
steps.action: Areas are three x and six.
steps.narration: The second region is three times two, not two.

steps.title: Verify with the given input
steps.action: At four the whole rectangle measures six by three.
steps.narration: Its area is eighteen square centimetres.

worked_examples.verify: At x=4 area 3(4+2)=18 and 3(4)+6=18; claimed 14 is wrong.
worked_examples.misconception: The learner forgets to multiply the extra length by the width.
worked_examples.repair: Highlight both rectangles with a shared height of three.

worked_examples.skill: Audit two orderings of a flow
worked_examples.q: Rule A triples n then subtracts 2; Rule B subtracts 2 then triples. A learner says both rules give the same output. Test n=4 and write both rules.
worked_examples.answer: A(n)=3n−2 gives 10; B(n)=3(n−2) gives 6; they differ.

model.description: Audit two orderings of a flow

states: Two flow rules; learner claims equality

steps.title: Trace A in order
steps.action: Triple four to twelve then subtract two to ten.
steps.narration: The subtraction happens after multiplying.

steps.title: Trace B in order
steps.action: Subtract two first to get two then triple to six.
steps.narration: The bracket groups the subtraction before multiplying.

steps.title: Compare one shared input
steps.action: Ten differs from six, so the universal claim fails.
steps.narration: A single counterexample is sufficient.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner ignores the order of flow operations.
worked_examples.repair: Place both flows in parallel lanes and track the same input.

worked_examples.q: A learner writes 2(3z−4)−(z+1) → 6z−4−z+1 → 5z−3. Name the first incorrect operation, simplify, and check at z=2.
worked_examples.answer: First error: 2(−4) should be −8. Correct result 5z−9; at z=2 both original and result equal 1.

steps.title: Find the first illegal product
steps.action: Two times minus four is minus eight, not minus four.
steps.narration: Stop at the earliest incorrect arrow.

steps.title: Expand the second bracket
steps.action: Subtract z and also subtract one.
steps.narration: The minus sign applies to both terms.

steps.title: Collect after both repairs
steps.action: Six z minus z is five z; minus eight minus one is minus nine.
steps.narration: Keep variable and constant lanes separate.

steps.title: Check the original at two
steps.action: Original is two times two minus three, which equals one.
steps.narration: Five times two minus nine also equals one.

worked_examples.misconception: The learner misses two distribution signs; the first is 2×(−4).
worked_examples.repair: Repair the first illegal arrow, then continue every bracket term.

practice_questions: Is 4a+3b=7ab valid? Give the simplest correct expression.
Unlike a and b terms remain separate.
The signed coefficients are +9 and −5; their sum is 4.
The outside minus changes both terms.
Square only the variable in brackets.
Write √(u²) valid for every real u.
Is 4(x+1) equivalent to 4x+1? Give the correct expansion.
Distribute four to each bracket term.
A learner expands 3(2w−5) as 6w−5. Correct the first error.
Simplify (8r²+12r)/(4r) and state the excluded value.
Check the original denominator before dividing.
For r≠0 the two quotient terms are 2r and 3; r=0 is undefined.
A taxi costs R9 once and R6 per kilometre. Give C(d) and C(3).
For three kilometres cost is R9+R18=R27.
A rectangle has sides (s+4) cm and 2 cm. Find area and evaluate at s=3.
Split the length into s and four.
Flow A doubles t then adds 3. Flow B adds 3 then doubles. Give both outputs at t=2.
Follow each arrow in its own lane.
Distribute three and negative one separately.
mastery_questions: Eight x minus three x gives five x; y stays separate.
The original denominator is zero at b=0; for b≠0 the quotients are 2b and 3.
A booking costs R11 once plus R7 per seat. Give C(n) and cost for 4 seats.
Seven repeats four times: 28; add the one eleven-rand charge to get 39.
A learner writes 2(4p−3)−(p−5) → 8p−3−p+5. Identify first error; simplify and check at p=1.
First error: 2(−3)=−6; result 7p−1; at p=1 both equal 6.
Correctly distribute two then minus one: 8p−6−p+5=7p−1; original at one is 2(1)−(−4)=6.
reassessment_questions: A learner says 5(2q+1)=10q+1. Diagnose and repair.
Five multiplies two q and one; at q=1 both correct forms equal 15.
The original denominator 4c excludes zero. Divide both numerator terms by 4c.
A ticket costs R8 plus R3 per bag. Give C(b) and its value for 4 bags.
Four bag charges cost R12; add the one R8 ticket fee.
